27 July 2026

**Dear Editor,**

Please consider our manuscript, **“Resource-Aware Local–Global
Multi-Resolution Localization and Recovery on a Constrained RV1103 Embedded
Platform,”** for publication in your journal.

Reliable two-dimensional LiDAR localization on constrained embedded hardware
requires more than pose accuracy: an implementation must track physical
movement, detect loss, recover after displacement, tolerate short scene
disturbances, and remain within CPU, memory, and scan-cycle limits. Existing
studies often examine these requirements separately or only on host computers.
Our work connects the localization method, embedded implementation, physical
evaluation, and hardware-resource evidence in one auditable study.

The manuscript presents a five-state local–global multi-resolution
correlative localization system deployed on an RV1103 board–LiDAR platform;
RV1106 evidence is included only for supported conditions. Six traceable test
families comprise 24 reported, finalized sessions. RV1103 completed all 16
nominal route checkpoints with 0.0279 m position RMSE and 0.589° heading RMSE.
Four physical kidnapped trials recovered within 0.529–0.970 s, while twelve
dynamic-crossing windows accepted 472/475 scans and automatically recovered
from one brief loss.

Factor isolation explains the result: only the combined local–global,
multi-resolution variant recovered in both replay sources. On RV1103, the
selected method achieved approximately 49–50 ms matcher P95. Recorded-paced
replay measured 66.05% time-weighted CPU, 1,456 KiB peak RSS, and a 0.69%
computation-deadline-miss rate. Live measurements additionally expose
scheduling costs hidden by algorithm-only replay.

The manuscript is appropriate for a journal addressing embedded intelligent
systems, localization, sensor processing, and resource-aware edge computing.
Its contribution is a reproducible embedded co-design and evaluation relating
physical accuracy, recovery, disturbance response, method factors, and
hardware cost. Finalized evidence retains raw telemetry, configuration,
processed metrics, binary/map hashes, and SHA-256 manifests. Source code and
publication materials are maintained at
<https://github.com/hharyono/SLAM.git>.

Thank you for considering our manuscript. We appreciate the opportunity to
submit this work for editorial and peer review.

Sincerely,
